purpose: Material and thickness of every wall of this flat, established with the owner over 2026-09-04 from his own colour markup of the developer's basic plan plus the developer's building description. NOT derivable from the drawing: the plan uses the SAME hatch and the SAME thickness for concrete and for aerated block, so this is owner-supplied evidence.
status: Classification COMPLETE and owner-confirmed. Two thicknesses provisional (see provisional[]). NOT yet mapped onto shell wall names - that needs v0 geometry, which does not exist yet.

the_warm_perimeter.owner_concept: The owner's own framing, and it is the organising idea: there is a WARM PERIMETER - the thermal envelope of the heated flat - and it is UNIFORM in construction all the way round.
the_warm_perimeter.owner_words: «[M1] is external wall, and it is uniform, the same thickness across all the warm perimeter. M1 is the external wall with all the insulation, because [the лоджия] was envisioned as a cold area. It's not heated, it's outside of this external wall perimeter.»
the_warm_perimeter.build_up: 300 mm autoclaved aerated concrete block + 70 mm mineral wool on the OUTSIDE + render and paint (developer spec).
the_warm_perimeter.note: Non-load-bearing: the monolithic RC frame carries everything. That does not make them alterable in practice - they are the façade.
the_warm_perimeter.critical_consequence: !! THE ЛОДЖИЯ IS OUTSIDE THE WARM PERIMETER, AND THE WALL BETWEEN THE FLAT AND THE ЛОДЖИЯ IS PART OF IT - fully insulated, 300 + 70. See loggia_thermal_consequence below; it changes the frost-free calculation.

loggia_thermal_consequence.finding: !! THE ЛОДЖИЯ IS THERMALLY DECOUPLED FROM THE FLAT, AND THAT CUTS AGAINST THE OWNER'S OWN GOAL.
reasoning: The wall between the flat and the лоджия - M1, plus M7 and the insulated face of R8 - is full warm perimeter: 300 mm block with 70 mm of mineral wool.
So essentially NO heat leaks from the heated flat into the лоджия. One might otherwise have assumed some did.
M2 separates this лоджия from the neighbour's, and both are unheated - cold-to-cold, no help from that side either.
The лоджия's own enclosure is thin and uninsulated by design: M2 'thinner', M6b ~200 mm provisional.
The floor and ceiling are slabs shared with the loggias above and below, which are also unheated.
loggia_thermal_consequence.consequence: !! THE STANDING TARGET - keep the лоджия frost-free through an ordinary Belarusian winter with NO heating, on passive measures alone - therefore rests on exactly two things: SOLAR GAIN, and the лоджия's OWN enclosure. Nothing is contributed by the flat.
loggia_thermal_consequence.the_good_news: Solar gain is the best it could be: the лоджия's main angled glazing faces DUE SOUTH (confirmed orientation), making it the most solar-exposed element in the flat.
loggia_thermal_consequence.the_work: So the glazing upgrade the owner is already planning is doing nearly all of the work, and the thin uninsulated enclosure walls (M2, M6b) are the weak points. Whether the target is achievable at all is an open question the vault has already flagged as a content gap - see 00_Master/Family_Requirements.md section 10 - and this is the constraint set that question has to be answered against.
loggia_thermal_consequence.note_on_scope: The owner has decided NOT to join the лоджия to the flat and to keep its doors and windows. That decision is unaffected; what changes is where the heat has to come from.

what_this_cannot_do_yet: These ids are regions on a raster markup, not named walls in the model. Mapping them onto data/canonical/current_apartment_shell.json requires v0 geometry, which does not exist yet - so make_variant.py cannot enforce any of this today. Building v0 from the plan's printed linear chains is the blocking task.
